newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Coporo oil field called very promising.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Coporo oil field called very promising.

text.p: Colombia's newly discovered Coporo oil field has shown extremely promising results so far and may contain up to 2 billion barrels of high quality crude oil reserves, Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar was quoted as saying Thursday.

In an interview with El Tiempo, Colombia's leading daily, Villamizar said geologists estimated that the field was bigger than the massive Cusiana and Cupiagua development in the country's eastern plains, which boasts 1.3 billion barrels of proved reserves.
"It's bigger than Cusiana," he told El Tiempo.
When British Petroleum Co Plc discovered Cusiana four years ago it described the oil find as the biggest in the Western hemisphere since the late 1960s.
Last month in New York, President Ernesto Samper told a news conference that Coporo had about 700 million barrels of crude oil.
But Villamizar said the state oil company, Ecopetrol, has since drilled the full 18,000 feet of the first Coporo well and confirmed oil reservoirs in all three of its geological layers.
"We don't want to jump the gun, but the reserve estimates are much larger than had been said before," he told El Tiempo.
He said geologists now believed Coporo to contain 1.5 to 2 billion barrels of crude oil, although he fell short of calling this a commercial figure.
The Coporo field is located about 55 miles (90 km) east of Bogota, near both the Cusiana and Piedemonte fields.
